title: Email and the Internet
subtitle: check your email, go online, download
summary: Talk about sending email, going online and what people do on the Internet - searching, downloading, shopping and social networking.

lesson.heading: Using email
lesson.text: You **check your email** to see if you have any messages. You **reply to** the emails you **receive**, and you **delete** the ones you do not need. Emails that you do not want, usually adverts, are called **spam** or **junk mail**.

examples.text: I **check my email** about five times a day.
I try to **reply to** every message **immediately**.
I **delete** old emails **regularly**, because I get so many.
Most of my **spam** is advertising for things I never buy.
I sent you an email with an **attachment**.
examples.note: an attachment = a file sent with an email

lesson.text: We write an email address as pd@freeserve.co.uk but we say it: pd **at** freeserve **dot** co **dot** uk.

lesson.heading: Getting started on the Internet
lesson.text: To go on the Internet you need an **ISP** (Internet service provider). It will **connect** your computer to the Internet and give you **access to** email and other services. When you **go online** you can send and receive emails, or **browse** the Internet with a **browser** such as Internet Explorer, Firefox or Safari.

examples.text: Do you have Internet **access** at your school?
examples.note: access = the ability to use something

examples.text: When I **go online**, I usually read the news first.
If you **click** on a **link**, it takes you to a different website.

lesson.heading: Searching and downloading
lesson.text: Students **search the Internet** for information; we also say **do an Internet search**. People **download** information, pictures, music and **video clips** onto their computer. The opposite of download is **upload**.

examples.text: I **searched the Internet** for cheap flights to Rome.
Do you **download** much stuff from the Internet?
I watch **video clips** of football matches.
examples.note: a video clip = a small part of a video recording

examples.text: She **uploaded** her holiday photos to the website.

lesson.heading: Shopping online
lesson.text: People buy books, clothes and food **online**. They go to a website, **select the item** they want and click *add to basket*. When they have finished shopping, they go to **checkout** and pay for their items, usually with a **credit card**.

examples.text: **Select the item** you want and add it to your basket.
At the **checkout** I paid with my **credit card**.
You can also take out insurance **online**.

lesson.heading: Other things people do online
rows: a personal website with news about a subject, or about events in your life
a person who writes a blog
spend time looking at different websites
places on the Internet where you discuss things with other people, e.g. Facebook
leave messages for your friends on a website
sending and receiving messages in real time

exercises.prompt: Match the verb on the left with the words on the right.

exercises.explanation: An ISP connects your computer to the Internet and gives you access to email and other services.

exercises.prompt: What are Safari, Internet Explorer and Firefox?
exercises.explanation: You browse the Internet using a browser.

exercises.prompt: Emails that you do not want, usually advertisements, are called ___.
exercises.explanation: Spam is also called junk mail.

exercises.prompt: How do you say Zac@hotmail.com? Zac ___ hotmail dot com.
exercises.explanation: We say at for @ and dot for the full stop.

exercises.prompt: *A:* A friend of mine has got his own ___. *B:* Oh yeah. What does he write about?
exercises.explanation: A blog is a personal website about a subject or about your own life.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Do you always reply to emails ___? *B:* Yes. I think it's rude if you don't reply as soon as you receive one.
*A:* How can I view information about the computers they sell? *B:* Just click on that ___, and it will take you to the website with the details.
exercises.explanation: You click on a link to move to another website or another part of a website.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Do you have Internet ___ at your school? *B:* We do in school hours, but not before or after school.
exercises.explanation: Access = the ability to use something.

exercises.prompt: *A:* I sent you an email earlier with an attachment. Did you get it? *B:* Oh, I'm afraid I haven't ___ my email today yet.
exercises.explanation: Check your email = look to see if you have any messages.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Do you delete emails ___? *B:* Yes, every day. I receive so many, and most of them aren't important.

exercises.statement: When you upload music, you copy it from the Internet onto your computer.
exercises.explanation: When you download music, you copy it from the Internet onto your computer. Upload is the opposite.
